# typed-sql 2.3.0

typed-sql 2.3 adds shared JSON contracts, portable execution adapters, and compiled runtime value
plans. SQL syntax, coercions and diagnostics remain owned by the selected grammar.

## Highlights

- PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQLite carry bounded JSON shapes through constructors, aggregation,
  paths and supported mutations. Application declarations narrow types only when runtime
  validation is available. JSON null and SQL NULL remain separate at transport boundaries.
- `@typed-sql/adapters` adds explicit D1, libSQL, Neon HTTP/WebSocket and postgres.js entrypoints.
  Applications own their database drivers and client lifetimes. Adapters expose only native
  transaction, batch and control capabilities they can support.
- SQL-file factories and the Vite frontend attach executable value plans. Generated runtime
  imports resolve through portable grammar entrypoints without an extra application dependency
  on Core. Conditional and repeated SQL structures are checked against compiled evidence.
- Query composition preserves result validators. Copies that discard query metadata and generic
  executors without a transport contract cannot bypass compiled validation.
- Immutable plan preparation, row decoding and JSON validation allocate less. Repeated plans
  share owned immutable JSON shapes without relaxing expansion limits.
- Reproducible raw-driver and Reylo comparisons include cold and warm paths, prepared execution,
  concurrency, CPU and allocation evidence. Runtime validation has a measurable cost; these
  results do not establish a universal speed advantage.

## Compatibility

The stable runtime and compiler require Node.js 22.11 or newer. The optional `node:sqlite` adapter
requires Node.js 22.13 or newer. The optional Node SQL-file loader requires Node.js 24.11.1 or
newer on the Node 24 line, Node 25.1 or newer on the Node 25 line, or a supported later line.
PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite are stable dialect packages.

The ordinary compiler uses TypeScript 7.0.2. The isolated experimental editor backend uses
TypeScript 7.1.0-beta. Editor artifacts are exercised on Linux, macOS and Windows.

Dynamic repeated-fragment result properties remain conservatively nullable unknown. SQLite's
reviewed catalog range is 3.39.0–3.53.4; a newer bundled library, including SQLite 3.54 in Node 26,
retains conservative inference rather than inheriting unreviewed language guarantees.

See the [compatibility matrix](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/reference/compatibility),
[portable adapters](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/reference/portable-adapters), and
[upgrade guide](https://lojhan.github.io/typed-sql/guides/upgrading-from-v1).

## Package tracks

The stable package train contains `@typed-sql/core`, `@typed-sql/opentelemetry`, `@typed-sql/ast`,
`@typed-sql/schema`, `@typed-sql/config`, `@typed-sql/compiler`, `@typed-sql/conformance`,
`@typed-sql/postgres`, `@typed-sql/mysql`, `@typed-sql/sqlite`, `@typed-sql/cli`, and
`@typed-sql/adapters`.

`@typed-sql/ts-bridge`, `@typed-sql/language-server`, and the editor integrations remain
experimental. A shared release-candidate version does not promote their preview contracts;
stable packages do not depend on them.
